ety.text: Borrowed from Malay keris. Doublet of kalis. Recognized as part of English ca. 1580.

senses.d: A traditional Indonesian, Malaysian, or Filipino sword or dagger having a tapering, usually serpentine blade.
To stab or cut with a kris; to kill with a kris.
ex: [...] when I was a boy, but Rajah Sul and Sultan Abdel krissed and speared all the poor people and burned the campongs.
One Malay seaman had resisted the rattan halter––he had been krissed to death on the spot and thrown overboard.
